_readme: data/_schemas/system_registry.json — THE built-state source of truth.
WHAT THIS IS  The one file that answers 'is it built?'. CLAUDE.md's reading map
sends every fresh session here FIRST, before any prose doc. When a
doc and this file disagree, this file wins and the doc is stale.
WRITTEN BY    /map-systems (adds planned systems), /design-system (status on GDD
docs-sync: new tools, data categories, priority rotation),
SEEDED BY     the installer's scaffold step — valid, parseable, and EMPTY. An
empty registry is the correct day-one state; it fills as systems
land. Do not delete keys you have not used yet: a skill that finds
the key finds an empty list and moves on; a skill that finds no key

_schema_notes.phase: Mirror of production/stage.txt, kept here so a single JSON read answers 'where are we?'. stage.txt stays AUTHORITATIVE — /gate-check writes it. If the two ever disagree, believe stage.txt and fix this.
_schema_notes.systems: One object per system. Required: id, name, status, layer. Optional: priority, features[], dependencies[], decisions[] (ADR ids), gdd (path), notes. Example entry: {"id": "your-system", "name": "Your System", "status": "planned", "layer": "gameplay", "dependencies": [], "decisions": [], "gdd": "docs/gdd/your-system.md"}
_schema_notes.tools: One object per runnable tool the project owns: {"path": "tools/your_check.py", "purpose": "...", "run": "python tools/your_check.py"}. /consistency-check verifies every tool it finds on disk has an entry.
_schema_notes.data: One object per editable data category: {"dir": "data/your-category/", "schema": "data/_schemas/your_category_schema.json", "count": 0, "purpose": "..."}. Architecture principle 1 — content lives in data, never in scripts — is audited from here.
_schema_notes.documentation_stack: The doc ledger. active_docs[] = every live doc's path + role. spec_index.specs[] = every spec's state (in_progress | final | archived), file, archive_path, linked plan and ADR. adr_index.adrs[] = number, title, status, date, file. archived_docs[] = what moved to docs/z-old/ and when.
_schema_notes.next_session_priorities: Ordered array; [0] is what happens next. /update rotates it at ship time; /help and /sprint-plan read it. Entry shape: {"title": "...", "why": "...", "workstream": "...", "added": "YYYY-MM-DD"}.
_schema_notes.flagged_for_designer_review: Open contradictions the automated checks cannot resolve. Entry shape: {"id": "FLAG-001", "severity": "high|medium|low", "summary": "...", "raised": "YYYY-MM-DD", "report": "docs/open-flags.md", "resolved_in_commit": null}. Mirror the human-readable version in docs/open-flags.md.
_schema_notes.live_test_notes: How to actually run and see the thing today. current_focus is the one-liner /consistency-check compares against the top devlog entry.
_schema_notes.recently_changed: Append a dated array key per ship — recently_changed_YYYY-MM-DD: ["what changed"]. /regression-suite globs recently_changed_* to decide what needs a regression test. No dated key exists on day one because nothing has changed yet.
_schema_notes.status_vocabulary: See _status_meanings. Use exactly these words — skills match them as strings.

_status_meanings.planned: Decided and on the map; no code yet.
_status_meanings.stub: A placeholder exists that compiles/loads but does nothing real.
_status_meanings.partial: Works for the main path; known gaps remain.
_status_meanings.phasing_out: Superseded by another system; still present so nothing breaks.
_status_meanings.deprecated: Kept only for compatibility; do not build on it.
_status_meanings.for_review: Built, but its behaviour needs a designer verdict.

_edit_policy: Skills update this file as part of their normal run — no permission prompt for status/index changes. ASK before deleting a system entry or rewriting next_session_priorities wholesale; those are designer-owned decisions.

documentation_stack.boundary_rule: A doc belongs to exactly one owner skill. If two skills write the same doc, one of them is drifting.
